content: Polyethylene glycol-electrolyte solution (PEG-ES) is a laxative approved by the FDA for bowel cleansing prior to a colonoscopy. It is commonly associated with side effects such as abdominal bloating, fullness, and nausea. For adults, the solution can be administered orally at a rate of 240 mL (8 ounces) every 10 minutes until the rectal effluent is clear or a total of 4 liters is consumed. Alternatively, it can be given via a nasogastric tube at a rate of 20-30 mL per minute (equivalent to 1.2-1.8 liters per hour). Off-label uses in adults include oral administration of 1 liter in two 500 mL portions over 4-6 hours or 1000 mL every 45-75 minutes. For pediatric patients aged 6 months or older, the oral dosage is 25 mL/kg/hour until the rectal effluent is clear, with rapid consumption of each portion preferred. The same dosage applies for nasogastric tube administration. Use in children under 2 years of age requires careful monitoring for hypoglycemia, as the solution contains no caloric substrate. The product is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to any of its components, ileus, gastrointestinal obstruction, gastric retention, bowel perforation, toxic colitis, or toxic megacolon. It should be used cautiously in patients with severe ulcerative colitis and in children under 2 years of age. Patients with impaired gag reflex, unconscious or semiconscious states, or those prone to regurgitation or aspiration should be closely monitored during administration, especially if given via a nasogastric tube. If severe bloating, distention, or abdominal pain occurs, administration should be slowed or temporarily stopped. The most common adverse reactions include nausea, abdominal fullness, and bloating, which occur in up to 50% of patients. Less frequent side effects include abdominal cramps, vomiting, and anal irritation. Rarely, allergic reactions such as urticaria, rhinorrhea, dermatitis, or anaphylaxis have been reported. Serious adverse events, such as upper gastrointestinal bleeding, esophageal perforation, asystole, pulmonary edema, and aspiration-related complications, have been documented in older patients. Oral medications taken within one hour of starting PEG-ES may not be absorbed due to rapid gastrointestinal transit. The solution is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning its effects on fetal development are unknown, and it should only be used during pregnancy if clearly necessary. There is no specific guidance for its use during labor, delivery, or in nursing mothers. Safety and efficacy in pediatric patients aged 6 months and older are supported by clinical trials and published studies, but there is no specific guidance for geriatric patients, gender, race, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised individuals. PEG-ES works by inducing diarrhea to cleanse the bowel, typically within four hours. Its osmotic activity and electrolyte composition prevent significant fluid or electrolyte imbalances, even with large volumes. The product is supplied as a white powder for reconstitution, containing polyethylene glycol 3350, sodium bicarbonate, sodium chloride, and potassium chloride. Flavor packs can be added to improve palatability. The solution should be refrigerated after preparation and used within 48 hours. Patients should be counseled to prepare the solution as directed and to avoid solid food for 3-4 hours before drinking it. Adults should consume 240 mL every 10 minutes until the stool is clear, while pediatric patients should drink 25 mL/kg/hour. Rapid consumption is preferred. The first bowel movement typically occurs about one hour after starting the solution. If severe discomfort or distention occurs, the rate of consumption should be slowed or temporarily stopped. Alcohol interactions with PEG-ES have not been established, and patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while taking this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name TRILYTE®.
